security_audit.summary: The skill documents legitimate Svelte CLI workflows, but several locations instruct agents to run @sveltejs/mcp through npx. Most static hits are Markdown backtick false positives; the real review concern is external npm CLI execution against docs, inline code, or local file paths.

remediation.suggestion: Pin @sveltejs/mcp to a reviewed version or install it as a project dependency with a lockfile before running commands.

remediation.issue: Shell handling for inline code and paths
remediation.suggestion: Avoid interpolating untrusted code into shell strings. Prefer reviewed file paths, strong quoting, or argument arrays when invoking the CLI.
Limit autofixer runs to intended Svelte project files and avoid paths that may contain secrets or unrelated private data.

content.value_statement: Svelte 5 syntax and runes can be hard to verify during component edits. This skill guides agents to fetch docs and run focused autofix checks.
actual_capabilities: Lists available Svelte 5 and SvelteKit documentation sections through @sveltejs/mcp.
Retrieves selected documentation sections after section discovery.
Runs the Svelte autofixer against inline component code or a file path.
Supports Svelte 4 or Svelte 5 autofixer targets through the version option.
Reminds users to escape rune symbols when passing inline code through a shell.
limitations: Requires command execution with npx and npm package availability.
Does not edit files by itself; it provides command workflows and analysis guidance.
Autofixer results depend on @sveltejs/mcp behavior and the installed package version.
Shell quoting remains the caller's responsibility for inline code and file paths.

use_cases.title: Verify Svelte 5 Components
use_cases.description: Check rune usage, documentation alignment, and common component issues before final review.

use_cases.title: Support Svelte Migrations
use_cases.description: Compare Svelte 4 and Svelte 5 autofixer targets when planning incremental migration work.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Fetch relevant docs and run autofixer checks before commenting on Svelte code changes.

prompt_templates.title: Find Relevant Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to list Svelte documentation sections, then identify the sections for Svelte 5 state and derived values.

prompt_templates.title: Review Component Syntax
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to fetch docs for Svelte 5 effects and review my component for common rune mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Run Autofixer On File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to run the Svelte autofixer on a component file, target Svelte 5, then summarize issues by severity.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Migration Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare Svelte 4 and Svelte 5 autofixer output for a migration candidate and recommend a migration plan.

output_examples.input: Review a Svelte 5 counter component that uses runes.
output: Relevant docs to fetch: state, derived values, and effects.
Autofixer checks should validate rune usage and event handling.
Final feedback should separate required fixes from optional cleanup.

output_examples.input: Check a SvelteKit file before a pull request review.
output_examples.output: The skill would look up the relevant documentation, run the autofixer on the intended file, and summarize warnings for review.

output_examples.input: Prepare a Svelte 4 component for a Svelte 5 migration.
output_examples.output: The skill would compare version-targeted autofixer results and identify migration concerns that need manual testing.

best_practices: Pin or install @sveltejs/mcp in the project when repeatability matters.
Fetch documentation before changing unfamiliar Svelte 5 patterns.
Run the autofixer before finalizing component or module edits.
anti_patterns: Running npx commands from an untrusted directory or without reviewing package provenance.
Passing unescaped inline code through a shell when it contains rune syntax.
Treating autofixer output as a replacement for tests or manual review.

faq.question: Does this skill write Svelte code?
faq.answer: It guides documentation lookup and autofixer checks. The agent still performs any code edits separately.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: The npx workflow may need npm registry access unless the package is already installed or cached.

faq.question: Can it support Svelte 4?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented autofixer command supports a Svelte 4 target through its version option.

faq.question: Is it safe to run?
faq.answer: It uses external commands. Review package provenance, pin versions, and avoid passing sensitive files.

faq.question: Does it access hidden files?
faq.answer: No evidence found. The detected hidden-file issue is a reference to Svelte file extensions.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is marked as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
